caption:
You can have a Riviera holiday without spending it behind the wheel. Pick a base in Nice, unpack once and let the coastal trains open up the rest. 🚆

Keep a day for Nice itself: a slow walk along the Promenade des Anglais, an old-town lunch and nowhere urgent to be.

Then choose one seaside town per outing:
• Antibes, west of Nice: wander the old town, stop at a café and loop back along the ramparts.
• Villefranche-sur-Mer, east: take the old village lanes down to the harbour, then leave room for Marinières beach.
• Menton, farther east: stroll Les Sablettes below the colourful old town, with the Saint-Michel steps an optional detour.

TER services link these towns with Nice. Antibes is in the opposite direction from Villefranche and Menton, so this is a set of separate day trips—not a four-stop day. Check your travel dates and last return trains before setting out; stations still involve a walk to the places pictured.

These photographs are warm-weather inspiration. Beach and swimming days depend on the season and conditions; the waterfront walks and town outings can be the trip in their own right.

Save this for the group chat that wants a little more coast and a little less organising.

Photos: Luna Wang, Nick Page, Chelsea Essig & Leonardo Caetano / Unsplash.

editorial_intent: A French Riviera escape based in Nice, using coastal trains for separate day trips to Antibes, Villefranche-sur-Mer and Menton, with long lunches, old-town walks and time beside the sea.
share_reason: Friends can choose one hotel base and a different seaside outing each day, enjoying the Riviera without hiring a car or packing up between towns.
